title: Learning Lotteries with Minimal Stakeholder Violations from Membership Queries
abstract: arXiv:2610.37828v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An AI developer often has several candidate versions of a system and can deploy a mixture of them, sending each request to a randomly chosen version, as in A/B testing. Each stakeholder (e.g., a safety team, a regulator, or a customer with private test data) accepts a mixture exactly when its expected performance (e.g., its rate of harmful replies) meets the stakeholder's own standard, which the developer can learn only by asking whether a proposed mixture is acceptable. We model this as choosing a lottery over $m$ alternatives for $n$ agents, each of whom accepts exactly the lotteries in an unknown halfspace and answers such binary membership queries. While Choo et al. (ICML 2026) sought a lottery that every agent accepts, none may exist when, say, safety and helpfulness requirements conflict, so we minimize the number of rejecting agents. translated_title: 基于成员查询学习使利益相关者违反数最少的彩票方案
translated_abstract: AI 开发者通常拥有一个系统的多个候选版本，并且可以部署它们的混合方案（如同 A/B 测试），将每个请求发送到随机选择的版本。每个利益相关者（例如安全团队、监管机构或拥有私有测试数据的客户）只有在混合方案的期望性能（例如有害回复的比率）满足其自身标准时才接受该方案，而开发者只能通过询问某个提议的混合方案是否可接受来了解这些标准。我们将此问题建模为：为 n 个智能体在 m 个备选项上选择一个彩票（lottery），每个智能体恰好接受位于某个未知半空间内的彩票，并回答此类二元成员查询。虽然 Choo 等人（ICML 2026）寻求每个智能体都接受的彩票，但当例如安全性与有用性要求发生冲突时，这样的彩票可能不存在，因此我们转而最小化拒绝者的数量。我们证明了即使在所有半空间已知且所有效用满足特定条件的情况下，该问题也是 APX-难的。
tldr: 该论文将部署 AI 系统多个候选版本的混合方案问题建模为在未知半空间偏好下为多个利益相关者选择彩票，通过二元成员查询学习各方接受标准以最小化拒绝的利益相关者数量，并证明该问题即使在偏好完全已知时也是 APX-难的。
en_tdlr: This paper models deploying a mixture of AI system versions as a lottery selection problem for stakeholders with unknown halfspace preferences, learns their acceptance criteria via binary membership queries to minimize the number of rejecting stakeholders, and proves the problem is APX-hard even when all preferences are fully known.
